input.title: Tunde Adebayo — ETH Zürich MSc Data Science statement
input.body:
I am applying to the ETH Zürich MSc Data Science because I want advanced training that connects machine learning with real engineering systems and prepares me for applied research. My BEng in Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Covenant University gave me a foundation in signals and systems, probability and statistics, linear algebra, control systems, and digital signal processing. I completed a final-year project on edge inference for low-cost power-quality sensors.

Since January 2024, I have worked as a machine-learning engineer at GridSense Africa, where I have built load-forecasting pipelines and anomaly-detection prototypes for distribution networks. This work has strengthened my interest in reliable machine learning for infrastructure and in methods that can operate under limited data and imperfect sensing conditions. I have also submitted the manuscript “Self-supervised event detection for weak distribution grids” to IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid on 4 May 2026; no decision has been received.

My goal is to develop the theoretical and practical depth needed for applied machine-learning research, particularly for energy and other infrastructure systems. ETH Zürich’s data-science environment is a strong fit for this direction. I would bring an engineering perspective, experience with Python, PyTorch, embedded C, signal processing, and MLOps, and a commitment to careful, reproducible work.

I can self-fund tuition up to £18,000 and would need support above that amount. I have no disciplinary history.
